comment: What the IDE acceptance test expects. `displayed` is the text the IDE grid paints with its default formats, observed on the Java reference; `rows` is what the JS API returns. app.d/ide_tables.py builds these tables on Java.

ticking.comment: The last `rows` ticks of a counter: N is consecutive and grows, Sq is N squared. Timestamp is not compared (it is painted in the browser's time zone).
ticking.name: ide_ticking

console.comment: Route (a): the commands typed into the IDE console, per console type. Each creates the two tables under other names.

python.static: from deephaven import new_table, time_table; from deephaven.column import int_col, string_col, double_col; ide_console_static = new_table([int_col('Id', [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]), string_col('Sym', ['AAPL', 'MSFT', 'GOOG', 'AMZN', 'OXHV']), double_col('Price', [101.5, 202.25, 303.125, 404.0, 505.75])])

errors.comment: Route errors: `fail` raises an error with the text `{marker}` after an assignment, and the console then shows `shows`; `create` makes the table `gone` out of what `fail` assigned, and `remove` removes the variable while its panel is open.

python.create: from deephaven import new_table; from deephaven.column import int_col; ide_errors_gone = new_table([int_col('Gone', [ide_errors_before, ide_errors_before + 1])])

grid.comment: Route grid: a table of 300 rows, K = 0..299 and G = K % 7, made in the console; more rows than a viewport holds. `top` and `bottom` are its first and last painted rows; `sort.top` after sorting K descending; `filter.top` after also filtering G to the value of the first row.

python.create: from deephaven import empty_table; ide_grid = empty_table(300).update(['K = (int)ii', 'G = (int)(ii % 7)'])

grid.name: ide_grid

log.comment: Route log: a command that prints `{marker}`, which the test replaces with a text of its own.

notebook.comment: Route notebook: the lines typed into a new notebook, per console type. The last line runs by itself (Run Selected) and makes the table `selected`; the whole notebook (Run) also makes the static table under another name. `comment` starts a comment of the language.

lines: from deephaven import new_table; from deephaven.column import int_col, string_col, double_col
from deephaven import new_table; from deephaven.column import int_col; ide_notebook_selected = new_table([int_col('Sel', [7, 8])])

rollup.comment: Route rollup: the command typed into the console makes a table of six rows; the Rollup Rows panel of its grid makes a rollup of it by `groupBy`, with the options of `without` unchecked. `collapsed` is what the grid paints at first (the grand total and the first level), `expanded` what it paints after a click on the row of `expand`, `sort.rows` after sorting `sort.column` descending from its header, `filter.rows` after also filtering by the cell number `filter.cell` of the row of `filter.value`, with the entry `filter.entry` of the menu Filter by Value. Observed on the Java reference.

commands.python: from deephaven import new_table; from deephaven.column import int_col, string_col; ide_rollup = new_table([string_col('Sym', ['AAPL', 'AAPL', 'MSFT', 'AAPL', 'MSFT', 'GOOG']), string_col('Ex', ['N', 'Q', 'N', 'N', 'Q', 'Q']), int_col('Qty', [10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60])])

tree.comment: Route tree: the command typed into the console makes a tree of five rows, which the IDE opens. `collapsed` is what the grid paints at first (the rows without a parent), `expanded` what it paints after a click on the marker of the row of `expand`, `sort.rows` after sorting `sort.column` descending from its header, `sort.expanded` after another click on the marker, `filter.rows` after also filtering by the cell number `filter.cell` of the row of `filter.row`, with the entry `filter.entry` of the menu Filter by Value: the row and its ancestor. Observed on the Java reference.

commands.python: from deephaven import new_table; from deephaven.column import int_col, string_col; ide_tree = new_table([string_col('Id', ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e']), string_col('Parent', [None, 'a', 'a', None, 'd']), int_col('V', [10, 20, 30, 50, 40])]).tree('Id', 'Parent')
